Note: The free end A is on the left, the fixed support B is on the right, and x is measured from A. The beam is drawn to scale, so a longer beam is drawn longer. The reaction arrows only show direction and are the same size for every problem.

Part AReactions and maximum values

How to use the drawing tools

Reading the grid. Each vertical gridline is 1 ft along the beam. The horizontal gridlines are labeled on the left, and the heavy line in the middle is zero. Move your mouse over the grid and the readout above it shows the x and value of the nearest intersection. Points snap to intersections, so you can't place one off the grid.

  • Point: click a grid intersection to place a point where the diagram changes.
  • Horizontal: click two points at the same height to connect them with a flat line.
  • Vertical: click two points at the same x to connect them with a straight up-and-down line.
  • Diagonal: click two points at different x and different heights to connect them with a straight sloped line.
  • Curved: click two points, then choose which end of the curve is flat ("left point" or "right point").
  • Erase: click a point or a line to remove it. Erasing a point also removes the lines attached to it.
  • Undo / Clear: Undo reverses your last change. Clear wipes the grid (Undo brings it back).

For the line tools, the first click picks the starting point (it appears automatically, so you don't need the Point tool first) and the second click finishes the line. Click the same point twice to cancel.

Part BDraw the shear diagram, V(x)

Part CDraw the moment diagram, M(x)
